examples.en: I saw a wild cat on the mountain path.
Wild cats run away quickly when they see people.
Do a lot of wild cats live on the hill behind the village?
You shouldn't feed wild cats.
House cats and wild cats have very different eyes.
I hear a wild cat crying every night.

explain: 도시 골목에서 사는 고양이는 보통 '길고양이'라고 하고, '들고양이'는 산이나 들에서 사람 손을 타지 않고 사는 고양이를 말할 때 써요. 집고양이와 대비해서 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Cats living in city alleys are usually called '길고양이', while '들고양이' is used for cats living in mountains or fields without human care. It often appears when contrasting with house cats.

examples.en: In autumn, wild chrysanthemums bloom along the road.

examples.ko: 들국화 향기가 정말 좋아서 한참 맡았어요.
examples.en: The wild chrysanthemums smelled so good that I sniffed them for a while.
Grandmother picked wild chrysanthemums and put them in a bottle.

examples.ko: 산에 올라갔다가 들국화 사진을 많이 찍었어요.
examples.en: I climbed the mountain and took a lot of photos of wild chrysanthemums.
Wild chrysanthemums grow well even in cold weather.

examples.ko: 노란 들국화가 언덕 가득 피어 있어요.
examples.en: Yellow wild chrysanthemums are blooming all over the hill.

explain: '들국화'는 한 가지 꽃 이름이라기보다 산과 들에 피는 국화 비슷한 가을꽃을 두루 부르는 말이에요. 노래나 시에서 가을의 느낌을 줄 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '들국화' is not the name of one exact flower but a general name for chrysanthemum-like autumn flowers that grow on hills and fields. It often appears in songs and poems to give an autumn feeling.

examples.en: If you grind perilla seeds and put them in soup, it tastes nutty.

examples.ko: 엄마가 시장에서 들깨 한 봉지를 사 오셨어요.
examples.en: Mom bought a bag of perilla seeds at the market.
I want to eat perilla noodle soup.
We planted perilla in the field and it is growing well.
If you press oil from perilla seeds, it becomes perilla oil.

examples.ko: 들깨 향이 강해서 저는 조금만 넣어요.
examples.en: The perilla smell is strong, so I add only a little.

explain: '들깨'는 참깨와 다른 식물이에요. 씨를 갈아 국이나 나물에 넣고, 기름은 '들기름', 잎은 '깻잎'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: '들깨' is a different plant from sesame (참깨). The seeds are ground into soups or side dishes, the oil is called '들기름', and the leaves are called '깻잎'.

examples.ko: 길가에 이름 모를 들꽃이 피어 있어요.
examples.en: Wildflowers whose names I don't know are blooming by the road.
Don't pick wildflowers, just look at them.

examples.ko: 봄이 오면 들꽃 구경하러 산에 가요.
examples.en: When spring comes, I go to the mountains to see wildflowers.
Even one small wildflower makes my mind feel at ease.

examples.ko: 들꽃은 화단의 꽃보다 더 강해 보여요.
examples.en: Wildflowers look tougher than flowers in a flower bed.
The children made flower rings out of wildflowers.

explain: 사람이 가꾸지 않아도 산과 들에서 저절로 피는 꽃이에요. 반대로 사람이 심고 가꾸는 꽃은 '화초'라고 해요.
explain_en: These are flowers that bloom on their own in mountains and fields without anyone tending them. Flowers that people plant and care for are called '화초'.

examples.en: The autumn fields turned golden.
A wide stretch of fields passed by outside the train window.
Farmers are harvesting rice in the fields.
The spring breeze blows across the fields.
There are many greenhouses in the fields of my hometown.

examples.ko: 노을 진 들녘을 걸으니 마음이 편안해요.
examples.en: Walking through the fields at sunset makes me feel calm.

explain: '들판'과 비슷하지만 '들녘'은 풍경을 그리는 글이나 노래, 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '들판'이나 '논밭'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '들판', but '들녘' appears more in descriptive writing, songs and news. In everyday talk people usually say '들판' or '논밭'.

examples.en: The kids keep running in and out of the room.
The puppy is playing, going in and out of the yard.

examples.ko: 아침부터 사람들이 사무실에 들락날락 바빠 보여요.
examples.en: People have been going in and out of the office since morning and look busy.
My stomach hurt, so I kept going in and out of the restroom.
The person going back and forth in front of the shop looks suspicious.
Why do you keep going in and out of the house?

explain: '드나들다'보다 가볍고 짧게 자꾸 오가는 느낌이에요. 한 번 들어갔다 나가는 게 아니라 여러 번 반복하는 모습이에요. 비슷한 말로 '들랑날랑'도 있고, 화장실이나 문처럼 오가는 곳과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It feels lighter and quicker than '드나들다', with repeated coming and going rather than a single entry and exit. '들랑날랑' is a similar word. It goes well with places people pass through, like a restroom or a door.

examples.ko: 산 근처 들불이 번져서 소방차가 왔어요.
examples.en: A field fire near the mountain spread, and fire trucks came.
I heard there used to be a custom of setting fields on fire in spring.
The wind was strong, so the field fire spread in an instant.
Smoke from the field fire rose high into the night sky.
A field fire can start from a tiny spark.

examples.ko: 마른 풀이 많아서 들불이 나기 쉬워요.
examples.en: There is a lot of dry grass, so field fires break out easily.

explain: '산불'은 산에서 나는 불이고 '들불'은 들판의 풀밭에서 번지는 불이에요. 뉴스나 글에서는 불이 빠르게 번지는 모습을 '들불처럼'이라고 비유하기도 해요.

phrases.en: The rumor spread through the school like wildfire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소문, 운동, 유행이 아주 빠르게 퍼질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a rumor, movement or trend spreads very quickly.

explain_en: '산불' is a fire on a mountain, while '들불' spreads across grassy fields. In news and writing, '들불처럼' is also used as a comparison for something spreading fast.

en: ache all over; rummage through; stir up

examples.en: I have a cold, and my whole body aches.
My knees ache, maybe because it's going to rain.
Who rummaged through my drawer?

examples.ko: 지난 일을 자꾸 들쑤시면 싸움만 나요.
examples.en: If you keep stirring up the past, it only leads to fights.
I had body aches, and my joints throbbed all night.
I rummaged through my bag looking for the key.

explain: '쑤시다'와 비슷한데, '들쑤시다'는 몸 여기저기가 마구 아플 때나 물건과 일을 마구 뒤지고 건드릴 때도 써요. 몸이 아플 때는 '온몸이 들쑤시다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '쑤시다', but '들쑤시다' is used when pain is all over the body, and also when you rummage through things or stir up an issue. For pain, people often say '온몸이 들쑤시다'.

examples.en: The rice stuck to the pot, so washing it is hard.
Gum got stuck to my shoe.
The egg keeps sticking to the pan.

examples.ko: 책상에 들어붙은 스티커를 겨우 떼어 냈어요.
examples.en: I barely peeled off the sticker stuck to the desk.

examples.ko: 동생이 하루 종일 나한테 들어붙어 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling has been clinging to me all day.

examples.ko: 친구가 돈 많은 사람한테만 들어붙으려고 해요.
examples.en: My friend only tries to cling to rich people.

explain: '붙다'보다 꼭 달라붙어 잘 안 떨어지는 느낌이 강해요. 타서 바닥에 붙는 것은 '눌어붙다'라고 하고, 사람에게 들어붙으면 이익을 바라고 붙는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than '붙다', as if something clings tightly and won't come off. Food burnt onto a pan is '눌어붙다', and when used about people it has a negative sense of clinging for personal gain.

examples.en: On the icy road, the car slid and crashed into a roadside tree.

examples.ko: 졸음운전을 한 운전자가 앞차를 들이받는 사고가 났어요.
examples.en: There was an accident where a drowsy driver rammed into the car ahead.
The cow suddenly butted a tree with its horns.

examples.ko: 화가 난 염소가 울타리를 들이받고 있어요.
examples.en: The angry goat is butting the fence.
The bike crashed into a utility pole, and I got badly hurt.
If you talk back to the department head, work life gets hard.

explain: '부딪치다'는 그냥 닿는 것이고, '들이받다'는 머리, 뿔, 차 같은 것으로 세게 정면으로 박는 느낌이에요. 사람에게 쓰면 윗사람에게 대든다는 구어적인 뜻도 있어요.
explain_en: '부딪치다' just means to hit or bump, but '들이받다' means to slam head-on with force, using a head, horns or a vehicle. Used about people, it can colloquially mean to talk back to someone above you.

examples.ko: 밤에는 들짐승이 내려올 수 있어서 조심해요.
examples.en: Wild animals can come down at night, so I'm careful.
I heard a wild animal's cry deep in the mountains.

examples.ko: 들짐승은 겨울이 되면 먹이를 찾기 힘들어요.
examples.en: Wild animals have a hard time finding food in winter.
I heard the crops were damaged by wild animals.

examples.ko: 캠핑할 때는 음식을 들짐승이 못 찾게 잘 두세요.
examples.en: When camping, store your food so wild animals can't find it.

examples.ko: 이 숲에는 들짐승과 새들이 많이 살아요.
examples.en: Many wild animals and birds live in this forest.

explain: 산과 들에서 사는 야생의 짐승을 말해요. 집에서 키우는 '가축'과 대비되고, 새는 '날짐승'이라고 따로 불러요.
explain_en: It refers to wild beasts living in mountains and fields. It contrasts with livestock ('가축') kept at home, and birds are separately called '날짐승'.

examples.ko: 이 일은 날마다 퇴근 시간이 들쭉날쭉해요.
examples.en: In this job, my finishing time is different every day.

examples.ko: 머리를 직접 잘랐더니 길이가 들쭉날쭉해서 속상해요.
examples.en: I cut my hair myself and the length is uneven, so I'm upset.
My uneven grades are a worry.
I rewrote the uneven handwriting neatly.

examples.ko: 버스 배차 간격이 들쭉날쭉하면 기다리기 힘들어요.
examples.en: If bus intervals are irregular, waiting is hard.
The weather has been unpredictable lately, so bring a jacket.

explain: 길이, 시간, 성적, 날씨처럼 고르지 않고 들쑥날쑥할 때 써요. '들쑥날쑥'도 같이 쓰이고, 반대로 고르면 '일정하다'나 '고르다'라고 해요. 표면이 울퉁불퉁한 것은 '울퉁불퉁하다'가 더 어울려요.
explain_en: Use it when lengths, times, grades or weather are not even or consistent. '들쑥날쑥' is also used, and the opposite is '일정하다' or '고르다'. For a bumpy surface, '울퉁불퉁하다' fits better.

examples.ko: 지도에서 등고선이 촘촘하면 경사가 가파른 거예요.
examples.en: On a map, closely spaced contour lines mean the slope is steep.

examples.ko: 지리 시간에 등고선을 그리는 방법을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In geography class, we learned how to draw contour lines.

examples.ko: 등고선 간격을 보면 산의 모양을 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tell the shape of a mountain from the spacing of contour lines.

examples.ko: 등고선과 숫자를 보고 산 높이를 읽어요.
examples.en: I read the height of the mountain from the contour lines and numbers.
This contour line is drawn once every 100 meters.

examples.ko: 등고선 따라 난 길이라 오르막이 거의 없어요.
examples.en: The path follows a contour line, so there is almost no uphill.

explain: 지도에서 높이가 같은 곳을 이은 선이에요. 선 간격이 좁으면 가파르고 넓으면 완만하다고 읽어요. 지리 수업이나 등산 지도에서 주로 나와요.
explain_en: It is a line on a map connecting points of the same height. Narrow spacing means steep ground and wide spacing means gentle ground. It mostly appears in geography class and hiking maps.

examples.en: I met a friend on the way to school and we walked together.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 오늘 등굣길이 많이 막혔어요.
examples.en: It rained, so the road to school was very congested today.
The morning walk to school is always busy and hectic.

examples.ko: 아이들의 등굣길을 지켜 주는 어르신들이 계세요.
examples.en: There are elders who watch over the children on their way to school.
There was almost an accident at the crosswalk on the way to school.
There is a small bakery on my way to school.

explain: 학교에 가는 길이나 그 시간을 말하고, 반대말은 '하굣길'이에요. '출근길', '퇴근길'과 같은 짝으로 기억하면 쉬워요.
explain_en: It means the road to school or the time spent going there, and the opposite is '하굣길'. It pairs well with '출근길' and '퇴근길' in your memory.

examples.en: This chair has a high backrest, so it's comfortable.
May I tilt the backrest back a little?

examples.ko: 등받이 없는 의자에 오래 앉으면 허리가 아파요.
examples.en: Sitting a long time on a chair without a backrest hurts my back.

examples.ko: 차 등받이 각도를 바꿨더니 자세가 편해졌어요.
examples.en: I changed the angle of the car seat back and my posture got more comfortable.
I put a cushion against the backrest.
The backrest moves when you pull the handle.

explain: 의자나 자동차 좌석에서 등을 기대는 부분이에요. 팔을 올리는 '팔걸이'와 같이 의자 부분 이름으로 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is the part of a chair or car seat you lean your back against. It is good to learn it together with '팔걸이' (armrest) as chair-part names.

examples.en: Your posture looks good when your spine is straight.

examples.ko: 사람의 등뼈는 여러 개의 뼈로 이루어져 있어요.
examples.en: A human spine is made up of many bones.
I fell and almost hurt my spine.
I made pork bone soup with pork backbone.
The doctor checked the shape of my spine with an X-ray.
The backbone of a fish has many small bones.

explain: '척추'는 의학이나 설명할 때 많이 쓰고, '등뼈'는 일상에서 더 쉽게 말하는 표현이에요. 요리에서는 돼지 등뼈로 끓이는 감자탕처럼 재료 이름으로도 나와요.
explain_en: '척추' is common in medical or explanatory contexts, while '등뼈' is the plainer everyday word. In cooking it also appears as an ingredient, as in 감자탕 made with pork backbone.

examples.en: My rank went up a lot on this exam.
My rank is tenth in the class.
I decided not to compare ranks with my friend.

examples.ko: 등수에 너무 신경 쓰면 공부가 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you worry too much about rank, studying gets hard.

examples.ko: 달리기 시합에서 등수 안에 들지 못했어요.
examples.en: I didn't place in the running race.

examples.ko: 선생님이 등수 대신 점수만 알려 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher told us only our scores instead of ranks.

explain: '몇 등이냐'를 말할 때의 그 숫자를 가리켜요. 시험, 달리기, 대회 순위에 두루 쓰고, 학교 성적 순위는 '석차'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the number in 'what place did you get'. It works for exams, races and contests, and a school grade ranking is also called '석차'.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에는 소고기 등심을 구워 먹어요.
examples.en: Tonight we're grilling and eating beef sirloin.
Sirloin is a little fattier than tenderloin.
I made pork cutlet with pork loin.
Two servings of sirloin here, please.

examples.ko: 등심 스테이크는 중간 정도로 익혀 주세요.
examples.en: Please cook the sirloin steak medium.
Sirloin was on sale at the mart, so I bought a lot.

explain: 소나 돼지의 등 쪽 고기예요. 식당에서는 '안심', '갈비'와 함께 부위 이름으로 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It is meat from the back of a cow or pig. In restaurants you often hear it alongside other cut names such as '안심' and '갈비'.

examples.ko: 숙제 안 해서 엄마한테 등짝을 맞았어요.
examples.en: I didn't do my homework, so Mom smacked my back.
After working out, my back was soaked with sweat.
The baby fell asleep on Dad's back.
My back itches, could you scratch it for me?

examples.ko: 어깨 넓고 등짝 넓은 사람이 부러워요.
examples.en: I envy people with broad shoulders and a broad back.
It startles me when you hit my back all of a sudden.

explain: '등'을 낮추어 친근하게 부르는 말이라 가족이나 친구끼리 편하게 말할 때 써요. 격식 있는 자리에서는 그냥 '등'이라고 하는 게 좋아요. '등짝을 맞다, 때리다'처럼 혼날 때도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is a casual, slightly rough way to say '등' (back), used among family and friends. In formal settings just say '등'. It often appears when someone gets smacked, as in '등짝을 맞다'.

examples.en: The doorbell went ding-dong.

examples.ko: 딩동 소리가 나서 문을 열어 봤어요.
examples.en: I heard a ding-dong and opened the door.
I pressed the doorbell at the door and waited.
The ding-dong notification sound keeps coming.

examples.ko: 현관에서 딩동 소리가 나면 제가 나가 볼게요.
examples.en: If the doorbell rings at the entrance, I'll go see.

examples.ko: 엘리베이터에서 딩동 소리와 함께 문이 열렸어요.
examples.en: The elevator door opened with a ding-dong sound.

explain: 초인종, 알림음, 안내 방송처럼 맑게 울리는 소리를 흉내 내는 말이에요. 퀴즈에서 정답일 때 나는 소리는 '딩동댕'이고, 틀렸을 때는 '땡'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It imitates a clear chime such as a doorbell, notification or announcement. The sound for a correct quiz answer is '딩동댕', and for a wrong answer people say '땡'.

examples.en: When I got the quiz right, a ding-dong-dang sound played.
Wow, when you hear the ding-dong-dang sound, it's the right answer.

examples.ko: 아이가 딩동댕 하고 입으로 소리를 냈어요.
examples.en: The child made a ding-dong-dang sound with their mouth.

examples.ko: 문제를 풀 때마다 딩동댕 소리가 들려서 신나요.
examples.en: I hear ding-dong-dang each time I solve a problem, so it's fun.

examples.ko: 방송 프로그램에서 딩동댕 소리와 함께 정답을 알려 줘요.
examples.en: On the TV show, they reveal the answer with a ding-dong-dang sound.

examples.ko: 저는 딩동댕 소리를 들으려고 계속 맞혀 봤어요.
examples.en: I kept trying to answer correctly to hear the ding-dong-dang sound.

explain: 퀴즈 프로그램이나 문제 앱에서 정답일 때 나는 경쾌한 소리를 흉내 내요. 틀렸을 때 나는 소리는 '땡'이라고 해요. 정답을 말해 줄 때 장난스럽게 '딩동댕!' 하고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It imitates the cheerful sound for a right answer in quiz shows and study apps. The wrong-answer sound is '땡'. People also say '딩동댕!' playfully when confirming a correct answer.

examples.en: My throat stung, so I drank a lot of water.
The arm where I got the shot still stings.
Shampoo got in my eyes and they stung.

examples.ko: 약을 바르면 조금 따끔거릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: It may sting a little when you apply the medicine.
My sunburned skin stings, what should I do?
The mosquito bite stung and then started to itch.

explain: '따끔하다'는 한 번 찌르는 듯 짧게 아플 때 많이 쓰고, '따끔거리다'는 그 느낌이 계속 되풀이될 때 써요. 목, 눈, 상처, 피부처럼 쓰라린 곳에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: '따끔하다' is often used for a brief prick, while '따끔거리다' is used when that stinging feeling keeps repeating. It fits sore spots like the throat, eyes, wounds and skin.

examples.en: The spring sunshine is really warm and gentle.
I took a nap under the warm sunshine.
Today there was no wind and the weather was pleasantly warm.
Their gaze is always warm and kind.
The window side is warm, so the cat settled in.
The sunlight is warm, so it will be nice for a walk.

explain: '따뜻하다'와 달리 주로 햇볕, 봄볕, 따뜻한 눈길이나 마음처럼 부드럽고 포근한 것에 써요. 국이나 물처럼 뜨거운 것에는 어울리지 않고, 글이나 시에서 많이 보여요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '따사로워요'가 돼요.
explain_en: Unlike '따뜻하다', it is mostly used for soft, cozy warmth such as sunlight, spring light, or a kind gaze or heart. It doesn't suit hot things like soup or water, and appears often in writing and poems. It is a ㅂ-irregular, so it becomes '따사로워요'.

examples.en: This sentence was taken from a novel.

examples.ko: 발표 자료에 신문 기사를 따와도 돼요?
examples.en: Can I take from a newspaper article for my presentation?
I took the title from song lyrics.

examples.ko: 이름은 할아버지 이름에서 한 글자를 따와서 지었어요.
examples.en: We made the name by taking one character from grandfather's name.

examples.ko: 인터넷에서 그림을 따올 때는 출처를 써야 해요.
examples.en: When you take a picture from the internet, you must write the source.

examples.ko: 시에서 한 구절을 따와 카드에 적었어요.
examples.en: I took a line from a poem and wrote it on a card.

explain: 글, 노래, 이름 같은 데서 일부를 가져다 쓸 때 '~에서 따오다'로 많이 말해요. 같은 모양으로 '과일을 따 오다'(따서 가져오다)도 있으니 문장에서 뜻을 구분하세요.
explain_en: People often say '~에서 따오다' when taking part of a text, song or name to use elsewhere. The same form can also mean to pick fruit and bring it back (과일을 따 오다), so tell them apart by context.

examples.ko: 대화를 쓸 때는 따옴표를 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must use quotation marks when writing dialogue.

examples.ko: 따옴표 안에 친구가 한 말을 적으세요.
examples.en: Write what your friend said inside the quotation marks.
This sentence is missing quotation marks.
The part enclosed in quotation marks is a direct quote.

examples.ko: 소설에서는 따옴표 안에 인물의 말이 나와요.
examples.en: In novels, a character's words appear inside quotation marks.
Quotation marks come in pairs.

explain: 큰따옴표(" ")는 직접 말한 대화에, 작은따옴표(' ')는 마음속 생각이나 강조에 쓰는 게 기본이에요. 인용한 말을 표시할 때 가장 먼저 떠올리는 부호예요.
explain_en: Double quotation marks are basically for spoken dialogue, and single marks are for inner thoughts or emphasis. It is the first punctuation you think of to mark quoted words.

examples.en: I heard a woodpecker in the forest.
A woodpecker is pecking at a tree.
Woodpeckers make holes in trees with their beaks.

examples.ko: 산에서 딱따구리를 직접 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever seen a woodpecker in person in the mountains?
A woodpecker's beak is very hard.

examples.ko: 딱따구리가 만든 구멍에 다른 새가 살기도 해요.
examples.en: Sometimes other birds live in holes made by woodpeckers.

explain: 나무를 쪼아 구멍을 내는 새예요. 철자를 '딱다구리'로 잘못 쓰기 쉬운데 표준어는 '딱따구리'예요.
explain_en: It is a bird that pecks holes in trees. People often misspell it as '딱다구리', but the standard form is '딱따구리'.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 친구들과 딱지치기를 많이 했어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I played ttakji with friends a lot.

examples.ko: 딱지치기는 종이로 만든 딱지를 던져 뒤집는 놀이예요.
examples.en: Ttakjichigi is a game of throwing paper tiles to flip the other tile.

examples.ko: 동생이 딱지치기에서 제 딱지를 다 땄어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling won all my tiles in ttakji.
Do you want to play ttakji together?

examples.ko: 딱지치기를 잘하려면 손목을 잘 써야 해요.
examples.en: To be good at ttakji, you need to use your wrist well.
The kids are totally absorbed in ttakji in the alley.

explain: 종이를 접어 만든 '딱지'를 바닥에 내리쳐서 상대 딱지를 뒤집는 전통 어린이 놀이예요. '딱지'는 교통 딱지나 상처에 앉는 딱지 같은 다른 뜻도 있으니 문장에서 구분하세요.
explain_en: It is a traditional children's game in which you slam a folded paper tile (딱지) to flip your opponent's tile. '딱지' also has other meanings, like a traffic ticket or a scab, so tell them apart by context.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 늘 말을 바꾸고 딴소리해요.
examples.en: That person always changes their words and says something different.
What off-topic talk is this, suddenly in the middle of a meeting?

examples.ko: 약속해 놓고 이제 와서 딴소리하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't go back on your word now after you promised.

examples.ko: 질문에는 대답 안 하고 딴소리만 했어요.
examples.en: They didn't answer the question and only talked about something else.
Stop going off-topic and keep talking about what you were saying.
The child keeps talking about other things while doing homework.

explain: 지금 하는 이야기와 상관없는 말이나, 앞에서 한 말과 다른 말을 할 때 써요. '헛소리'는 말도 안 되는 소리라서 느낌이 달라요. '딴소리하다' 형태로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: Yesterday you said you'd go together, and today you're saying something different.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에서 한 말이나 약속을 뒤집을 때 써요. 불만스러운 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone reverses what they said or promised. It carries a tone of complaint.

explain_en: It means talk unrelated to the current topic, or saying something different from what was said before. '헛소리' means nonsense, so the feel differs. It is often used as '딴소리하다'.

examples.ko: 물을 마시다가 갑자기 딸꾹딸꾹 하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: I suddenly started hiccuping while drinking water.
The baby hiccuped and then stopped soon.

examples.ko: 너무 급하게 먹었더니 딸꾹딸꾹 소리가 나요.
examples.en: I ate too fast and now I keep hiccuping.

examples.ko: 딸꾹딸꾹 멈추지 않아서 물을 마셔 봤어요.
examples.en: The hiccups wouldn't stop, so I tried drinking water.

examples.ko: 조용한 교실에서 딸꾹딸꾹 소리가 울려서 부끄러웠어요.
examples.en: The hiccup sound echoed in the quiet classroom and I was embarrassed.

examples.ko: 숨을 참았더니 딸꾹딸꾹 하던 게 겨우 멈췄어요.
examples.en: I held my breath and the hiccuping finally stopped.

explain: 딸꾹질이 나는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. 증상 자체는 '딸꾹질'이라고 하고 '딸꾹질을 하다, 딸꾹질이 나다, 딸꾹질이 멈추다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound of hiccups. The condition itself is called '딸꾹질', used in phrases like '딸꾹질을 하다', '딸꾹질이 나다' and '딸꾹질이 멈추다'.

examples.en: The baby laughs while shaking a rattle.
The cat turned around at the sound of the rattle.
I bought a rattle as a gift for the baby.
A rattle makes a clear sound when you shake it.
Try getting the baby's attention with a rattle.
The rattle fell on the floor and the baby cried.

explain: '딸랑'은 작은 방울이 울리는 소리인데, '딸랑이'는 그 소리가 나는 아기 장난감이에요. 아기 용품 가게나 육아 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '딸랑' is the sound of a small bell, and '딸랑이' is the baby toy that makes that sound. It comes up often in baby shops and parenting talk.

examples.en: Our neighbors are a family rich in daughters, with five daughters.
A house with many daughters always has lots of laughter.
Grandmother has many daughters, so I hear holidays are fun for her.

examples.ko: 딸부자 집 막내로 자라서 언니가 셋이에요.
examples.en: I grew up as the youngest in a family of many daughters, so I have three older sisters.

examples.ko: 딸만 넷이라 딸부자라는 말을 자주 들어요.
examples.en: I have four daughters, so people often say I'm rich in daughters.

examples.ko: 요즘은 딸부자 집이 부러움을 받기도 해요.
examples.en: These days, families with many daughters are sometimes envied.

explain: 딸이 많은 집이나 그런 집 사람을 말해요. 여기서 '부자'는 돈이 많다는 뜻이 아니라 어떤 것이 풍성하게 많다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It refers to a family with many daughters, or a person in such a family. Here '부자' doesn't mean wealthy but carries the feeling of having plenty of something.

examples.en: My parents cherish their daughter dearly.
They say raising a daughter is a lot of fun.
My daughter is already a college student.

examples.ko: 딸자식 결혼식 날 아버지가 눈물을 보이셨어요.
examples.en: On his daughter's wedding day, Father shed tears.

examples.ko: 딸자식 걱정에 어머니는 밤새 잠을 못 주무셨어요.
examples.en: Worrying about her daughter, Mother couldn't sleep all night.

examples.ko: 외국에 사는 딸자식한테 매일 전화가 와요.
examples.en: I get a call every day from my daughter who lives abroad.

explain: '딸'보다 부모가 자기 딸을 말할 때 정과 무게가 느껴지는 말이고, 조금 예스러운 느낌도 있어요. 남의 딸을 높일 때는 '따님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Compared with '딸', it carries affection and weight when parents talk about their own daughter, with a slightly old-fashioned feel. To honor someone else's daughter, say '따님'.

examples.en: The workout clothes smell strongly of sweat.
The bus in summer was full of the smell of sweat.

examples.ko: 땀내 나는 옷은 바로 빨아야 해요.
examples.en: Clothes that smell of sweat should be washed right away.

examples.ko: 아빠 옷에서 땀내와 햇볕 냄새가 났어요.
examples.en: Dad's clothes smelled of sweat and sunshine.
I sprayed perfume on my clothes to get rid of the sweat smell.

examples.ko: 땀내는 빨래 후에도 남을 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes the sweat smell stays even after laundry.

explain: '땀 냄새'와 거의 같은 뜻인데 한 단어로 짧게 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '땀 냄새'가 더 흔하고, '땀내'는 글에서도 잘 보여요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '땀 냄새' but as one short word. In daily speech '땀 냄새' is more common, while '땀내' also shows up in writing.

examples.en: The baby got heat rash on the neck.

examples.ko: 더운 날 땀띠 때문에 너무 가려워요.
examples.en: On hot days, the heat rash makes me very itchy.

examples.ko: 땀띠에는 시원하게 씻고 말려 주는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: For heat rash, it's good to wash coolly and dry the skin.

examples.ko: 땀띠 연고를 바르니까 가려운 게 나아졌어요.
examples.en: After I put heat rash ointment on, the itching got better.

examples.ko: 땀띠 가루를 발라 주니 아기가 편안해 보여요.
examples.en: After I put powder on the heat rash, the baby looks comfortable.
They say heat rash forms when sweat pores get blocked.

explain: 더운 여름에 땀이 많이 나서 피부에 작게 돋는 발진이에요. 보통 '땀띠가 나다'라고 말하고, 아기들에게 많아서 '땀띠 가루'도 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is a small skin rash that appears when you sweat a lot in hot summer. People usually say '땀띠가 나다', and since it is common in babies, '땀띠 가루' (heat rash powder) is a good word to know too.

examples.en: Sweat stains appeared on my shirt and I was embarrassed.
Sweat stains show up easily on a gray T-shirt.

examples.ko: 땀자국을 없애려면 찬물에 먼저 빨아 보세요.
examples.en: To remove sweat stains, try washing in cold water first.
How do you remove sweat stains left on a pillow?

examples.ko: 옷 겨드랑이 쪽 땀자국 때문에 겉옷을 입었어요.
examples.en: I wore a jacket because of the sweat stains under my arms.

examples.ko: 땀자국 걱정 없이 입을 옷을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for clothes I can wear without worrying about sweat stains.

explain: 땀이 옷이나 베개에 배어 남은 자국이에요. '자국'은 '발자국', '눈물 자국'처럼 무언가 지나간 흔적을 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 여름철 옷 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the mark left when sweat soaks into clothes or a pillow. '자국' is used for traces left behind, as in '발자국' (footprint) and '눈물 자국' (tear mark). It comes up often in talk about summer clothes.
